title: Curriculum-Adaptive Task Decomposition for Multi-Agent Workflows
research_question: Can a multi-agent workflow controller that adapts task decomposition granularity online using failure patterns and task-difficulty curricula improve end-to-end success rate and reduce redundant agent calls compared with fixed decomposition strategies?
hypothesis: A controller that begins with coarse decomposition, detects recurrent failure modes, and selectively refines only hard subtasks will outperform fixed coarse or fixed fine decomposition by improving success on difficult tasks while lowering total token and agent-execution cost.
motivation: The knowledge base shows repeated rejected proposals around uncertainty-aware scheduling, adaptive replanning, verifier guidance, and multimodal debate agents, suggesting that common novelty patterns in agent orchestration are already saturated or insufficiently differentiated. A clearer gap is adaptive decomposition itself: existing rejected ideas reference verifier-guided decomposition, but not curriculum-based online control of decomposition granularity driven by observed failure trajectories. This targets a practical bottleneck in agentic systems—over-decomposing easy tasks wastes budget, while under-decomposing hard tasks causes compounding errors—without overlapping with previously rejected routing, calibration, or Bayesian-control ideas.
